To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the theory of electrode electron transfer with polarizable molecules in solution is formulated, and it is shown that the statistics of thermal activation is non-Gaussian due to the difference in polarizability of the reactant in the oxidized and the reduced states.

the theory of electron transfer between metal electrodes and polarizable molecules in solution is different from the classical Marcus-Hush model, and that the theory is based on two parameters, the reorganization energy of the oxidized molecule and that of the reduced one.
electrode electron transfer reactions with polarizable solute molecules are described by a two parameter non-Gaussian model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of redox electrode reactions involving electron transfer from a metal electrode to a polarizable molecule.
the study of the electrochemical properties of redox-active molecules in solution.
the development of new theory of electrochemistry that takes into account the molecular structure and dynamics of polarizable molecules in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new non-Gaussian model of electron transfer is presented and applied to electrode reactions.
the theory developed in this paper is a significant advance in the theory of electrode electron transfer reactions.
the new theory of electrode reactions involving polarizable molecules is more consistent with experimental data than the classical Marcus-Hush theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a theory of electrode electron transfer based on the Marcus-Hush theory has been formulated and that this theory predicts a number of new effects which can be tested experimentally.
the new theory provides a consistent and quantitative explanation for the observed deviations from the Marcus-Hush theory of electrode electron transfer reactions with polarizable reactants.
the new theory of electrode electron transfer provides a unified description for the kinetics of electron transfer between a polarizable molecule and an electrode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the non-Gaussian nature of the electrode reaction is a result of the polarizability of the reacting species and is not a consequence of electron correlation.
the non-Gaussian theory of electrode reactions is more consistent with experimental results than the Gaussian model.
the asymmetry of the Tafelian plots is a manifestation of non-Gaussian statistics of thermal fluctuations in electrode reactions.
